'''''Cyperus difformis''''' is a species of [[Cyperus|sedge]] known by several common names, including '''variable flatsedge''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=CYDI4|taxon=Cyperus difformis|accessdate=17 January 2016}}</ref> '''smallflower umbrella-sedge''' and '''rice sedge'''.<ref name=FloraBase>{{FloraBase|name=''Cyperus difformis''|id=789}}</ref> This plant is native to southern [[Europe]], most of [[Africa]] and [[Asia]], and [[Australia]], and it is naturalized in other areas of the world, including large parts of the Americas.<ref name=kathe>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=236342 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]{{Dead link|date=June 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=cyperus+difformis Altervista Flora Italiana, Zigolo delle risaie, Cyperus difformis L.] includes photos plus range maps for Europe and North America</ref><ref>Miller, A.G. & Morris, M. ''Cyperus difformis'' is a plant of [[aquatic plant|aquatic]] and moist habitats. It is a weed of [[Paddy field|rice fields]], but not generally a troublesome one. This is an annual herb with one to many thin, soft erect stems reaching over 30 centimeters in maximum height. There are usually a few long, wispy leaves around the base of the plant. The [[inflorescence]] is a rounded bundle one to three centimeters wide, containing up to 120 [[raceme|spikelets]], each long and partially or entirely covered in up to 30 [[bract]]ed flowers. The flowers are light brown with areas darker brown and sometimes a yellowish or purplish tint.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242101119 Flora of China, Vol. 23 Page 226, <big>异型莎草</big> yi xing suo cao, ''Cyperus difformis'' Linnaeus, Cent. Pl. 2: 6. 1756. ]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242101119 Flora of North America, Vol. 23 Page 156, ''Cyperus difformis'' Linnaeus, Cent. Pl. II. 6. 1756. ]</ref>

==Similar Species==
''C. difformis'' can be distinguished from most visually similar species by the small size of the glumes, 0.5-0.7 x 0.5 mm, resembling tiny slightly elongated blunt beads.<ref name="FEU">{{cite book |title=Flora Europaea |author=Tutin}}</ref>
